title: High-Speed Flywheel Energy Storage with Magnetic Bearing Suspension
abstract: A kinetic energy storage system comprising a carbon-fiber composite rotor at 50,000 RPM in vacuum, supported by active magnetic bearings.
claims: A flywheel rotor comprising carbon-fiber reinforced polymer with tensile strength exceeding 3 GPa.
Active magnetic bearing system with 5-axis control maintaining rotor position within 10 micrometers.
A vacuum enclosure maintaining pressure below 0.01 Pa.
problem_statement: Electrochemical storage degrades over cycles. Flywheels offer unlimited cycle life but face bearing friction and containment challenges.
